title: ELF//SHELL // Transmission Log
description: Official development transmissions, release notes and illustrated archive dispatches from ELF//SHELL — Ayarime.

items.title: Transmission 001 — A signal from Ayarime
items.summary: A permanent RSS channel for ELF//SHELL development notes, release announcements and the Illustrated Memory Archive. The channel is distinct from Firefox extension updates and does not report browser activity.

items.title: Transmission 002 — Ayarime enters public review
items.summary: ELF//SHELL — Ayarime v0.5.5 was submitted to Mozilla Add-ons for public (listed) review via the automated GitHub Actions release pipeline. The submission produced a Mozilla version record, but submission does not mean the extension has been reviewed, signed, or publicly published.

items.title: Transmission 003 — ClickUp Serviteur MCP: first public beta
items.summary: An illustrated eight-sliver dossier accompanies ClickUp Serviteur MCP v0.3.0-beta.1, first released as a public GitHub source prerelease on 7 November 2026. The article now includes a separately dated field guide to 80 current named MCP tools and an evidence-linked comparison with ClickUp MCP alternatives researched on Glama. It explains Serviteur's independent, self-hosted per-user OAuth approach, server-enforced resource scopes, distinct named operations and practical workflows, while acknowledging competitors' broader API coverage and specialist strengths. This remains an independent source beta, not a hosted service or an endorsement by ClickUp.

items.title: Transmission 004 — The Twin Archive: ClipMint on two desktops
items.summary: Ayarime's Twin Archive is an illustrated story and design journal for a planned coordinated release of ClipMint on Linux Mint and Windows x64. Both editions have independent codebases and local history; they do not synchronise data. Linux Mint already has preview builds, while Windows x64 has a complete development-signed alpha with a verified GitHub build. Neither is being announced here as a finished public beta: physical desktop testing, Linux illustration-rights review, and permanent two-platform release packages remain prerequisites. The two doors will open together only after both pass their release gates.
